data.name: FlatOut 4: Total Insanity
data.detailed_description:
FlatOut Is Back!

FlatOut 4: Total Insanity™, where reckless driving has never been this much fun.
FlatOut 4: Total Insanity™ blends everything everyone has ever loved about FlatOut into one offering. Gamers will also be introduced to all new and exciting features, game modes, and vehicles which will soon become personal favorites. Another installment of nitro fueled demolition and derby racing featuring a variety of tracks, modes, arenas and multi-player options are available. Welcome back to FlatOut!

Exclusive to STEAM version of FlatOut 4: Total Insanity™
• Big Picture Mode
• Steam Achievements
• Partial Steam Controller Support
• Steam Leader Boards
• Steam Cloud
• Steam Trading Cards
• Exclusive Arena: Ice Lake Arena
• 2 Exclusive Drivers: Gadget Stewart and Dave Worker
• 2 Exclusive Vehicles: Ice breaker and Repair truck
• Steam Workshop coming 30 days post launch

FlatOut 4: Total Insanity™ Features
• High Speed racing and collisions on a variety of tracks and environments
• Customizable Cars: Gamers will unlock 27 cars to customize and race, including tributes to fan favorites and new additions to the garage
• Gamepad Controller Support
• Dynamic Tracks: FlatOut 4: Total Insanity™ features 20 tracks including traditional derby racing, time trials, arenas, assault levels, carnage levels and much more
• Destructible Environments: Chaos and destruction return to the world of racing with high speed collisions and wild destructible environments
• The Legendary Stunt Mode: Featuring 12 stunts in total. Six new stunts and six re-imagined classic stunt mini-games await fans in search of epic crashes and death-defying maneuvers
• Arena Mode: Three game play styles including Death Match, Capture the Flag and Survivor
• New Assault Mode: An arsenal of deadly weapons at your disposal to slow or destroy opponents
• Single Player: Race, Destroy and enjoy Stuntman mode offline before showing off your skills in multi-player
• Multiplayer Mayhem: Competitive online modes allow up to eight players to master destruction arenas, race courses and set traps
• Hot Seat Mode: Take turns with your family and friends in hot seat competition of Stunts
• Thumping Indie Soundtrack: FlatOut features a global range of over 35 amazing indie music tracks

• Male and Female Drivers: 12 Drivers: 6 males and 6 females:
• Classic
• Military
• Prisoner
• Punk
• Clown
• Hippie
• + 2 Exclusives: Gadget Stewart and Dave Worker
• Uses the power of next gen devices with high end 3-D rendering
• Sophisticated Physics engine based on Nvidia PhysX and KT Engine

reviews.review:
Let me just start with how great the audio and core gameplay is. Cars sound mean, crashes sound and feel brutal, the nitrous is crazy warpspeed, playlist is also pretty nice with a variety of rock/metal tracks that fits the theme, graphics also look good and has a familiar feel. It definitely harkens back to the older era of FlatOut. However what gave me a rather unsatisfying impression at first is the pseudo-softbody, difficult handling (mainly related to road surface sensitivity, and incredibly prevalent in the derby series), as well as the frustrating/chore progression that you can fall into.

It starts out pretty fun with a fairly easy to deal with AI, enabling you to enjoy the scenery whilst mashing your opponents and avoiding trees. However as the game carries on it sharply increases in difficulty. The cars are not easy to handle to begin with so add aggressive AI into the mix, and it gets rather frustrating to keep the momentum going without crashing out multiple times in game (and real life). Mid-game you're forced to upgrade to a faster car which is the legally distinct Jeep, but what you don't realize is how insanely difficult this car is to drive.

If you look at the community hub you'd notice how many memes there are about the physics, the Jeep being the center of it. Its short wheelbase makes it easy to spin out upon contact or misjudged corners, and the suspension is so sensitive that slight bumps will launch you into the sky. I did eventually try upgrading it to the max and this significantly reduces that issue, making it a pretty nimble rocket. Once the big old car unlocks, it does get a lot more fun. A tip I would share on driving is to slow down when you go through an unpredictably bumpy road and train rails. Honestly they could've polished this a little more so its less punishing.

You might ask why not just get another car? Well, first of all you can't sell cars like the older games. So naturally buying other cars and upgrading takes a lot of grinding so you're kind of stuck once you invest in a car until you saved up enough money again. Upgrades do help but its not really significant until you max out the car. However I would advise to be careful about the Gearbox upgrade. I made the mistake of upgrading the Gearbox on the Preacher (big old car) and now it feels sluggish. It wouldn't be an issue if there's a rollback function but there isn't.

There's also another factor I mentioned in the beginning with frustrating/chore progression. Unlocking cars is not as straightforward as I imagined it to be. Finishing the whole derby race doesn't unlock all the derby cars(?) It seems this is a way for us to actually play the whole series, but I wasn't aware of this and now I've finished the derby series without using the other cars that I've been eager about. Apparently FlatOut mode also unlocks cars. They could've at least let us know somehow like an info on the locked cars or maybe even implement an XP system. I also honestly dislike the initial selection of cars, and getting stuck with them is frustrating but this is a personal preference in sportier cars. 

Finishing races also feels like a lifetime so I sometimes dread having to drive on certain difficult tracks. My tip is to not try and get all gold like I did, just win enough to get money to buy/upgrade cars and move on to the other series. The fun begins when you go full nitrous and plow through your opponents and send them flying, but this requires a quick and sturdy enough car that you'd get in the later series.

This one's not really a dealbreaker but the characters are not quite there. They look kind of odd with their awkward mugshots and I don't really feel any sort of attachment since they don't come with backgrounds or have a distinct enough driving style like the older games. They're just reskins of the same 2 male/female model. I just end up just feeling indifferent about them and it only feels like they are a drivatar we can earn.

So anyway, why do I still recommend it? Honestly I still kind of like it. It tries to go back to its roots, and in the later parts of the game like the Classic & All Star series it does become more fun than frustrating. Cars are faster to recover and its definitely insane when you start boosting into oblivion. The Survivor race (demolition) and FlatOut mode (stunts & etc) is also quite fun. And technically you can play casually with Quick Play though stuff will be locked until you finish up Career & FlatOut mode. So if you got no problem with grinding at the beginning you'll be rewarded with quite the chaotic and fun experience later on.
